events.title: The encyclical Pacem in Terris
events.shortBlurb: On Holy Thursday, a dying John XXIII addressed his great letter on peace to all people of good will…
body: On 11 April 1963, Holy Thursday, Pope John XXIII signed 'Pacem in Terris', his eighth and last encyclical, which he called his Easter gift. Written six months after the Cuban Missile Crisis, during which the Holy See had served as a channel between Washington and Moscow, it was the first encyclical addressed not only to the bishops and faithful but to 'all men of good will'.

Drafted with the help of Monsignor Pietro Pavan, the letter argued in four parts that peace on earth can stand only upon the order God laid down: the rights and duties of the human person, the right ordering of public authority, equality and mutual respect among nations, and a world community able to serve the universal common good, with disputes settled by negotiation rather than by recourse to arms.

John died of cancer less than two months later, on 3 June 1963. Read far beyond the Church — the first papal encyclical printed in full in the New York Times, and two years later the subject of a United Nations conference of statesmen and scholars — it remains a cornerstone of modern Catholic social teaching.
